title: THE LOCKDOWN EVENT FLOOR. d_score's perimeter vector prices a man against ~0.31 of EVENT production (rimprot, perimdisrupt, drb) he may never generate, so a stopper who does not gamble, block or rebound cannot pass 80 at any perdef. Each of the three event bars is now paid at max(its own bar, the class's own lower quartile x t), t ramping over the non-big pool's OWN perdef p95->p99 (85 -> 96). A floor, never a replacement: no card is lowered and a gambler keeps every point of his own production. Joe Dumars '90 DEF 74 -> 81, OVR 74 -> 78

THIS ROUND'S EDIT IS CONFINED TO d_score's PERIMETER VECTOR, between the `_rp_w` line and `_size`. It touches no weight — only the three event VALUES the vector reads — so it folds cleanly beside a round that changes d_bigness/is_big (179) or o_score (182, 184).

THE CLASS IS NOW PAID FOR EVENTS IT DID NOT GENERATE, and a later round that raises the perimdisrupt ATTRIBUTE for this same class would be paying it twice: the floor is a max(), so it recedes on its own as the real bar rises, but a round that moves perdef for these cards moves the floor with it (t is a function of perdef alone).

notes: THE SUBJECT, DECOMPOSED BEFORE THE ROUND. Joe Dumars '90, All-Defensive FIRST team, perdef 93, read DEF 74. His perimeter vector: perdef 0.62 x 93 = 57.45, rimprot 0.13 x 8 = 1.02, perimdisrupt 0.11 x 19 = 2.05, drb 0.07 x 3 = 0.21, discipline 0.05 x 92 = 4.84 — sum 65.56 after the 0.9743 size modifier at 6'3", x 1.1305 = 74.12. THE TERM THE RULING IS ABOUT is not perdef, which is already near the top of the board: it is the 0.31 of the vector that pays EVENTS, of which he collects 3.3 out of a possible ~31.

WHY IT IS A CLASS AND NOT A CARD. Of the 205 non-big cards at perdef >= 90, the seven lowest DEF are six Dumars seasons plus Raja Bell '07 (1st team, perdef 90, perimdisrupt 8, DEF 73); the eighth, Quinn Buckner '80, is five clear at 78. Bruce Bowen '04-'09 (perdef 97-99, perimdisrupt 23-34) is the same defect one band up, and this round lifts him with them — the scout cited Bowen '05 at 87 as a comparable, and he was under-read for exactly the same reason, only less far.

WHY A FLOOR AND NOT A WEIGHT SHIFT, measured. Moving weight from the event bars to perdef reaches the number too, but it is a change to EVERY perimeter card on the board including the 178 anchors, and it would take the gambler's own production away from him — which is the half of his ruling that says Bradley and Beverley stay where they are. max() reaches only the cards the ruling is about: 54 of 10,000, every one of them UP, and the four peers he named move by 0, 0, +1 and 0.

THE FOOTPRINT: 54 DEF movers, all up, max +7; 40 OVR movers, all up, max +4; ZERO movers on OFF, on marg, and on every one of the 17 attributes (0 of 10,000 sheets differ). The top 12 by DEF is identical, name for name and value for value. Beyond the scout's seven the class it reaches is exactly the class it is written for: Bruce Bowen '04-'09, Chris Paul '09-'17 (four-time All-Defensive 1st team at 6'0" with rimprot 4-13), Gary Payton '94-'01, Michael Cooper '85-'89, Sidney Moncrief '84-'86, Dennis Johnson '82/'83, Rajon Rondo '10/'11, Marcus Smart '19-'23, Maurice Cheeks '85, Jason Kidd '02, Jrue Holiday '23/'24, Luguentz Dort '25 — lockdown guards, every one.

WHAT THE FLOOR DOES NOT DO, which is most of it. At perdef <= 85 (94.9% of the non-big pool) t is zero and the vector is byte-identical to recal_80's. Above it the floor still only binds where the card's own bar is BELOW its class's lower quartile, so Jordan '89, Kawhi '16, Kobe '03/'08, Doug Christie '03, Jrue '21, Amen Thompson and Herbert Jones — every elite perimeter defender who also generates events — are byte-identical too.

THE FIVES. Ten champion/all-time/custom levels change a player's card and two change their roster: the All-time Pistons five now takes Joe Dumars '90 over Cade Cunningham '26 (ladder round 5 -> 8) and the All-Stoppers custom takes him over Mookie Blaylock '95 (ladder round 1 -> 2, swapping with All-Defense). The Pistons '89 and '90 champion levels keep ladder rounds 17 and 16.
All 178 anchors pass (0 failing, mean |error| 0.79), 436 tests pass, and all nine tactics taxes re-ratify unchanged through the harness.
